members.reason: ["No citable end source in the packet. The order suspends the Eight-Hour Law provisions for the duration of the national emergency proclaimed by Proclamation 2914; that emergency does not end by its own terms within the order's life. The end that applies is statutory: sections 203 and 204 of Pub. L. 87-581 (76 Stat. 357, approved Aug. 13, 1962, effective sixty days after enactment) repealed sections 1 and 2 of the Act of Aug. 1, 1892 as amended Mar. 3, 1913, the provisions this order suspended, with a continuing proviso for contracts existing on the effective date. That statute is held only as an unregistered source-ladder text (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/opus-refetch_https_www.govinfo.gov_content_pkg_STATUTE-76_pdf_STATUTE-76-Pg357.pdf_a0da22ffea.txt) and the dossier's citable later-event list for this order is empty. A source supplement registering that text is required; the registered clause span also needs an inventory correction because it begins in front-matter of the Federal Register issue."]

["No held text states the closing date of the 83rd Congress's term (under U.S. Const. amend. XX, sec. 1, noon on January 3, but that text is not held); the held House session-dates page (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11065_87th_Congress_term_dates_1961-01-03_to_1963-01-03_and_U.S._Const._amend._XX_sec._1_fo_1629d9be9b.txt) lists session dates only, is not registered evidence in this packet and supports no exact end date. The order's own-terms end during the 83rd Congress therefore has no dated, citable end source. EO 10566 (1954-09-29, held and citable) strikes 1952 and inserts 1953 in this order, a later amendment event and not an end."]

["The order's own terms end it at the close of December 31, 1953 (it closes agencies and excuses employees on half days of December 24 and December 31, 1953), and no later instrument was found; the end is not in doubt on the text. The claim cannot pass the claim checker's verbatim-quote test: the registered original is the pdfplumber recheck text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10508.recheck.txt), but the checker searches the clause-drafts recorded text for the same PDF, whose OCR is letter-spaced, so no quotation from the registered text is found there (0 of 378 words). Needed: the registered original text and the checker's searched text must be the same held bytes (register the recheck text with the source catalogue used by the checker, or re-prepare the packet on the recheck text)."]

Independent review did not uphold this version: [{"field": "whole_order_end.date, operative_clauses[EO:10514#whole].first_end (date and mechanism own_terms_performed_on_stated_effective_date)", "claim_says": "1953-12-31: the revocation was performed and the clause spent at the close of business on December 31, 1953; signing and filing are alternative readings", "source_says": "The order was signed 'Jantiary 19, 1954' and filed 'Jan. 20, 1954; 10:29 a.m.'. Its sentence 'This order shall become effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953' gives the revocation retroactive effect: it fixes when EO 2414 is treated as ceasing. It cannot fix when EO 10514's own command was performed, because the order did not exist on that date. The claim records this order's end 19 days before its issuance, so the lifecycle ends before it begins. The earliest end the source supports for EO 10514's command is its issuance (signing 1954-01-19, or filing 1954-01-20); 1953-12-31 is the end of the revoked order, not of this one."}]

["No held source shows an end. The order vests the Secretary of the Navy's interest in and control over moneys deposited in a Treasury suspense account under EO 10426 in the Secretary of the Interior hereafter, with the moneys to be expended or deposited as the Submerged Lands Act and the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act provide. A performed-on-issuance reading is not supported: the held 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10525.txt) reproduces the order among the texts that still had general effect on January 20, 1989, and no held source shows the suspense-account moneys were exhausted or the transfer revoked or superseded afterwards. Needed: a source after 1989 (or a statute or order) showing how the vesting ended. The dossier also notes that its current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256."]

["No held source ends the delegation. The statutory basis, section 806 of the Supplemental Appropriation Act, 1954 and section 737 of the Department of Defense Appropriation Act, 1955 (Pub. L. 458, 83d Cong.), is not held, so its expiry or repeal cannot be dated. The five chain events in the dossier (EO 11171, 11605, 11785, 13467, 13764) attach to EO 10450 printed on the same OCR page, not to this order. EO 12107 (printed 44 FR, Jan. 3, 1979) section 2-101(b) lists EO 10549 among orders amended by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission, an amendment and not an end, and the held 1989 OFR codification note under EO 12107 cites EO 10549 without a revocation notation. Needed: the instrument or statute that ended the delegation, with its text held. The registered clause span also includes neighboring Federal Register contents (clauses sec3-j and sec3-j-dup2)."]

["EO 10700 (signed 1957-02-25, held and citable as actor text) section 6 supersedes EO 10483 and the provisions amendatory of it contained in other Executive orders, which reaches this amendment, but its section 7 makes that effective on July 1, 1957 unless funds appropriated for the National Security Council were not then available for the Board, in which case on the later date they became available. No held source shows whether the funds were available on July 1, 1957, so no exact first-end date can be recorded. EO 10700 was later amended (by EO 10773 of July 1, 1958 and EO 10838) and revoked by EO 10920, whose text is held but not citable from this packet. Needed: a held source for the availability of the National Security Council funds, or another dated source for the effective date of EO 10700."]
